excerpt.quote: **Scientific adequacy: qualified.** The analysis provides a defensible whole-brain-corrected test of the supplied participant gain-effect coefficients and appropriately separates the vmPFC hypothesis from the posterior visual-cortex finding. The qualification is about missing-coverage handling: `analysis.py` defines support from finite, nonzero voxels, retains voxels with support from at least 90% of participants, then uses every participant value at those voxels. Any zero representing absent spatial coverage is therefore included as a measured zero; no explicit participant coverage masks are supplied to distinguish an actual zero coefficient from outside-analysis support. At most five of 54 maps can lack support at a retained voxel. This may pull a group estimate toward zero, and the supplied evidence cannot establish whether it does so in the vmPFC or elsewhere. The report discloses the 90% rule but describes it as accommodating variation rather than explaining this zero-as-observation assumption. This warrants qualification, not rejection of the analysis.

conclusion.quote: Reported hypothesis outcome:** no positive vmPFC effect is supported by this analysis under the required whole-brain-corrected inference. The anatomical ROI mean is −0.0041 (95% t interval −0.0250 to 0.0169; descriptive one-sided uncorrected p=.651), and no voxel in the AAL3v2 vmPFC approximation is in the positive max-T FWE significant mask. The whole-brain maximum is in posterior occipital cortex (t=6.62, pFWE=.00060); it does not support the vmPFC claim. This is lack of corrected evidence at the analysis's precision, not evidence that the true effect is exactly zero.
